ai.description: *Fejervarya orissaensis* is a small frog (30–40 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale vertebral stripe. It features a distinct, dark triangular mark between the eyes and prominent skin ridges.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Fejervarya orissaensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent white mid-dorsal line running from the snout to the vent.
ai.habitat: *Fejervarya orissaensis* typically inhabits lowland agricultural fields, marshes, and grassy wetlands in peninsular India, generally at altitudes below 500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Orissa frog is primarily nocturnal and terrestrial, often emerging after rainfall to forage for small invertebrates among leaf litter and damp vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Fejervarya orissaensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying large clutches of eggs in shallow, temporary water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Fejervarya orissaensis* is found along the eastern coast of India, primarily across the states of Odisha and West Bengal, typically inhabiting low-elevation plains.
ai.callDescription: The Orissa Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "chirp" pulses, typically heard emanating from shallow water bodies and flooded paddy fields during the monsoon.
